full_judgment:
Md Abdul Matin J : In this Rule the plaintiff-petitioner challenged the judgment and decree dated 11-10-1998 passed by the Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Chittagong in Money Appeal No. 25 of 1996 modifying those dated 21-7-1996 passed by the subordinate Judge, 3rd Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong in Money Suit No. 37 of 1994 decreeing the suit in part. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filing joint written statement and submitted that the defendants are not at all liable for any discharge of the Tallow from the ship. The trial Court decreed the suit in full and on appeal the appellate Court modified judgment of the trial Court and held that the plaintiff is entitled to get the price of 0.747 MT of goods as per law and survey report. 

 4. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the appellate Court the plaintiff petitioner moved the Court and obtained the present Rule. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that as per international survey the carrier is bound to deliver actual amount of the goods received from the exporter. In support of his submission he has referred to the case of Trans Oceanic Steamship Co Ltd and another vs Adamjee Insurance Co Ltd and another reported in 46 DLR 23 and in the case of Dula Meah vs Md Ibrahim Khalil alias Ibrahim Khalil reported in 37 DLR 93. On the other hand, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that if there is conflict between the 2 reports, Ullage Survey Report on board the vessel must prevail on the report of the Shore Tank Survey and the appellate Court rightly gave the plaintiff decree in respect of shortage as per Ullage Survey Report and committed no error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. In support of his contention, he has referred to the case of James Finlay PLC vs Member (Appeal) & Revision and Ext Office Additional Secretary to the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. Ministry of Finance. Dhaka and others, reported in 1990 BCR 194 and in the case of Trading Corporation of Pakistan vs Intercontinental Oceanic Enterprises Corporation and others (The NITSA") reported in Lloyds Law Reports at page 563. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the 2(two) decisions have no manner of application in the present case because those cases are under section IV of the Customs Act, 1969 and the Customs Act has nothing to do with the loss suffered by the importer. We find that a general principle has been accepted in the reported cases as mentioned that in the event of conflict between 2 reports one by Ullage Survey Report and the other by Shore Tank Survey Report the Ullage Survey Report shall prevail. We have nothing to differ with such finding by the writ Bench and accordingly, we do not find that any failure of justice has been caused by the appellate Court by modifying the judgment of the trial Court.
